subject: Renewal + scale playbook: NimbleHealth Dedicated pool uplift
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>

Cc: Devon Carter <devon.carter@nimblehealth.com>

Subject: Renewal planning — projected QPS growth and dedicated pool questions

Hi Karthik,

Our renewal for Dedicated capacity comes up in July and we want to lock in a plan that covers the next 12 months. A few notes from our side:
- Baseline production QPS right now is ~18 QPS (95th pct), average response tokens per request ~320.
- We're expecting a feature ramp in Q3 that could push peak QPS to 38 QPS and raise average tokens toward 420 by Q4.
- We need predictable throughput for our payer flows (latency SLO 300ms p95).

Can you recommend a reserved pool size (GPU count + instance type) and whether we should add burst capacity? Also need clarity on billing when we exceed reserved QPS and how preemption or fallback to hosted models would work.

Attached: export of last 30 days metrics (nimble_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx).

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, NimbleHealth

3) Any regulatory constraints that require private-only routing for certain regions?

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — projected QPS growth and dedicated pool questions

Hi all — I dug into the spreadsheet and ran a conservative capacity model. Key assumptions:
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (A100 80GB equivalent, quantized runtime assumptions) = 22k tokens/sec under multi-tenant batching profile we expect for Nimble.
- Typical request = 350 tokens (interim between current 320 and projected 420).
- Targeted operational headroom = 25% above 95th pct projected QPS to avoid queuing under bursts.

Forecasts (12-month renewal window):
- Current baseline (May 2026): 18 QPS * 350 tokens = 6,300 tokens/sec steady at 95th pct.
- Q3 ramp (expected): 28 QPS median projection → 9,800 tokens/sec.
- Q4 peak projection: 38 QPS → 13,300 tokens/sec.

GPU recommendation rationale (reserve + burst):
- Reserve pool sizing target: cover Q3 median + 25% headroom = 9,800 * 1.25 = 12,250 tokens/sec. At 22k tokens/sec per GPU, that maps to 0.56 GPUs → round up to 1 GPU.
- But Q4 peak 13,300 tokens/sec → requires 0.61 GPUs. For predictable throughput and maintenance overhead reduction we recommend reserving a minimum pool of 2 GPUs (A100-eq) for the 12-month term. This gives ~44k tokens/sec raw capacity and preserves headroom for unseen load patterns, model updates, and autoscaling constraints.
- Burst capacity: enable an immediate +2 GPU burst pool (pay-as-you-go when used) to cover simultaneous customer spikes and background eval jobs.

Operational notes:
- We propose per-route throughput guarantees scoped to the payer flows with an SLO target of 300ms p95 on the reserved pool. If traffic exceeds reserved sustained capacity, automatic routing to burst pool or graded fallback to a thinner model variant will be triggered per the runbook.
- We will instrument a gradual canary: week 0–2: 50% routing to reserved pool; week 2–4: 75% -> 100% subject to latency regressions.

Attachments: nimble_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (I added a sheet with per-GPU assumptions), draft_mpa_with_terms_v2.pdf (initial MPA with proposed reserved counts and burst pricing).

If Nimble wants to optimize cost, an alternative is 1 GPU reserved + 1 GPU spot-like burst with higher throttling tolerance; that reduces commit spend ~28% but increases risk of p95 violations during sustained peaks.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the math.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — projected QPS growth and dedicated pool questions

Thanks Lauren — helpful breakdown. Two clarifications from our side:
1) The table implies a single GPU could technically handle baseline loads, so why recommend 2 GPUs reserved? We want to balance cost and risk.
2) How is burst billing handled if we go over reserved capacity for short windows (e.g., sustained 90s bursts)? Is there a per-minute metering threshold or is it prorated hourly?

Also — we run overnight batch jobs that will touch the same models (model evals and nightly scoring). Would those consume reserved capacity during business hours if scheduled poorly? How do we isolate those workloads?

Cheers,
Devon
VP Engineering, NimbleHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Devon Carter <devon.carter@nimblehealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — projected QPS growth and dedicated pool questions

Hi Devon — answering both Qs inline and summarizing an operational playbook: 

1) Why 2 GPUs reserved vs 1: short answer — operational resilience and model-change risk.
- While one GPU might cover the steady-state token budget by pure compute math, it leaves no cushion for node maintenance, OS-level pauses, degraded kernel paths after a model update, or unexpected token size increases. For enterprise-grade SLA-backed Dedicated customers we recommend the extra headroom so we can confidently guarantee 300ms p95.
- Practically: 2 GPUs reduce queuing and allow rolling restarts/OS patches without client-visible impact.

2) Burst billing & metering:
- Burst billing is metered per-second aggregated across the burst pool and prorated to the nearest 60s window. Short spikes (under 120s) are billed at the burst per-GPU minute rate with a 60s minimum. Sustained usage beyond 15 minutes triggers an auto-suggest to convert burst consumption to a temporary invoiceable overage or prompt a capacity amendment.

3) Isolating overnight jobs:
- We recommend scheduling batch jobs into a dedicated background route bound to a separate pool (background-pool) with preemptible capacity. This prevents batch work from contending with payer-flows in the reserved/premium pool. Connor will include this in the rollout docs.

Proposed next steps: 
- Nimble approves: reserve 2x A100-eq GPUs for 12 months + enable burst pool (2 GPUs) with the metering terms above.
- Sign MPA v2 (I attached the draft) with a commit amendment clause allowing capacity changes at quarter boundaries with 30 days notice.
- Start canary on Aug 1 (alignment with your Q3 feature ramp).

Please reply with approval or any edits to the proposed billing rules and we can convert the draft MPA to a signature-ready copy.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30min call tomorrow if helpful.

—
